title: The Afternoon Brief: Progress reports pile up as Sunday deadlines approach
dek: Saturday's stories tracked forward motion across several sports: Ohtani's throwing progression, Scheffler's lead into the final round, and a wave of results and disciplinary rulings from rugby, AFL, and track. Sunday brings direct answers to several of these threads.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Several open questions from the morning now point to specific Sunday checkpoints: Scheffler's final round, Hunt's mixed relay, and Ohtani's next bullpen session.
bottom_line: Saturday's sports news was defined by progress toward pending outcomes: Ohtani's bullpen session moves him closer to a possible return, Scheffler's third-round lead sets up a final day he has not yet converted into a win this year, and Hunt's three golds leave one more race Sunday to complete a historic sweep. Elsewhere, the day delivered settled facts with real consequences: Witherspoon's record contract, the Wallabies' third straight win, and van Rooyen's three-match ban that could reach into Melbourne's finals. The Tarling story in Portugal remains the day's most serious open matter, with the reporting establishing what happened but not yet why. Sunday brings direct answers on the golf final round and the mixed relay, while Ohtani's next bullpen session and any findings on the Portugal incident remain the checkpoints to watch beyond that.
body: The day's clearest thread is that Saturday produced incremental progress rather than resolution, across sports that will each answer their open questions within a day or two. Ohtani's bullpen session, Scheffler's third-round lead, and Hunt's three golds all represent steps toward outcomes still pending, while other stories, the Witherspoon contract, the Wallabies' win, the van Rooyen suspension, delivered settled facts that now shape what comes next.

On the injury and return-to-play side, Shohei Ohtani threw a 35-pitch bullpen session Friday, his first mound work in more than three weeks since a July 3 left knee injury, and manager Dave Roberts said he is confident Ohtani will throw another bullpen session in two to five days. Separately, Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota suffered a sprained MCL in Friday's preseason opener against Miami and will miss the rest of the preseason, leaving Jayden Daniels as Washington's only available starter for now.

In golf, Scottie Scheffler shot 68 Saturday to reach 13-under 197, taking a two-shot lead over Sam Burns and Sungjae Im (both 11-under 199) into Sunday's final round at the FedEx St. Jude Championship. Scheffler is chasing his first win since January after five runner-up finishes this year, and he will be paired with Burns, his closest friend on tour, who beat him in a playoff at Colonial in 2022.

Elsewhere, results and rulings piled up. Australia beat Japan 56-17 in Townsville, its third straight Test win under new coach Les Kiss after trailing 21-17 at halftime. Devon Witherspoon signed a four-year, $132 million extension with the Seahawks, with over $101 million in guarantees, making him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. Melbourne forward Jacob van Rooyen was suspended three matches for a swinging-arm strike that knocked out Port Adelaide's Aliir Aliir, a ban that could extend into Melbourne's finals depending on ladder position. In track, Amy Hunt won her third gold of the European Athletics Championships and will attempt a historic fourth in Sunday's mixed 4x100m relay, while Dina Asher-Smith tied the championship record of seven career golds. And in Portugal, NSN withdrew its development squad from the Volta a Portugal after 19-year-old rider Finlay Tarling died Friday when a car reportedly entered the course against race direction.

The why behind most of these stories is straightforward and stated directly in the reporting: Ohtani's timeline follows a deliberate, staged recovery plan; Witherspoon's extension reflects a market re-set for cornerback pay after a championship run; van Rooyen's ban followed a formal match review process. The Tarling case is different: the reporting describes what happened but does not yet establish why the car entered the course or what safety measures may have failed, and that remains open pending any findings from race organizers or authorities.
No desk boards were available this cycle, so the picture here rests entirely on the day's published stories rather than a live scoreboard cross-check.

What to watch: Ohtani's next bullpen session, expected within two to five days per Roberts; Sunday's final round at TPC Southwind, where Scheffler tries to convert his lead against Burns and Im; Hunt's mixed 4x100m relay around 20:35 BST Sunday, where a win would make her the first athlete to win four golds at a single European Championships; any statement from Volta a Portugal organizers on course safety changes or an investigation into Tarling's death; and whether Melbourne appeals van Rooyen's suspension before the Demons' next match against the Western Bulldogs.
